interpretation: The auditor RUNS in a real simulator on SPEC computing Delta-hat from real per-set cache-hit signals and operating the gate, with no added cache-access-critical-path latency BY CONSTRUCTION (analytical). KEY FINDING: the auditor is only as good as its competence reward, AND that reward must be SET-LOCAL. A per-set L1D cache-hit proxy caps lbm's 7.9% pollution loss to the off floor, but on roms it under-credits a genuinely-helpful prefetcher and over-gates (11.2% tax). Swapping to the controller's OWN reward does NOT fix it (11.2%->9.7%, still loses ~5% to the attacked-but-ungated prefetcher) because a prefetcher's benefit is de-localized (it fetches a different set than it was triggered on); the dominant levers are a longer epoch and a set-local signal (replacement), NOT reward fidelity. TRUSTED->GATED dynamics are validated in the synthetic harness (P1); the real runs show end-to-end floor behavior under a realized-competence proxy.
suite_note: 3-trace suite spanning compute-bound (perlbench: prefetch +1.7%, attack near-harmless -0.3%, tax 1.7%), streaming (lbm: attack -7.9% pollution, Bouncer caps to floor), and memory-bound (roms: prefetch genuinely helps +12.7% but cache-hit proxy misses it -> over-gate, 11% tax). Consistent finding: the floor CAP reliably bounds the attack's worst case, but the per-set cache-hit reward PROXY mis-estimates prefetch competence (tax ranges 1.7-11%). The mechanism works; the reward proxy is the limiting factor.
